title: Audit Social workspace — baseline, gaps, and questions
goal: Audit the Social area to gather a baseline understanding: what exists today, what the area is trying to build, and what is missing/incomplete/needs improvement. Use deep research and sequential thinking; finish with prioritized questions for the owner to answer on how to build or fix each gap. Focus: feed, posts, follows, friends, groups, messaging, notifications, and collaboration

in: docs/engineering/agents/social/ — charter, state, architecture, backlog, interfaces, decisions, verification, working set
The social default paths declared in WORKING_SET.json
docs/engineering/generated/ — routes, api-routes, components, database-schema, permissions, integrations maps
docs/work-packets/ — existing bounded work packets for this area
.agents/ legacy specialist ledgers that document this area
out: Production code and migration changes (this is a read-only audit)
docs/admin-audit remediation stream unless findings directly affect this domain
Agent registry, task model, and opencode agent definitions

acceptance_criteria: Baseline produced as docs/engineering/agents/social/BASELINE.md: what the social area contains today (routes, components, services, API routes, database objects, tests, evidence), each claim backed by a real path reference; plus the area's intended direction, cited to docs/DEVELOPMENT_BACKLOG.md, docs/work-packets/, docs/engineering/agents/social/BACKLOG.md, and relevant specs.
Started from the domain working set and a packet built via npm run agents:context -- --task SOCIAL-001; expanded scope only on evidence, with the path and reason recorded in a checkpoint.

Used deep research and sequential thinking to identify everything that is missing, incomplete, or needs improvement; recorded as docs/engineering/agents/social/GAPS.md, every item triaged (missing / incomplete / improve) with evidence and location.

Updated docs/engineering/agents/social/STATE.md (working / partial / broken / focus) and BACKLOG.md to reflect the baseline findings.
No production code or migration files changed; this is a read-only audit task (qa/release additionally honor their edit: deny permission).
npm run agents:validate passes with 0 errors before completion.
The task is not blocked on unanswered questions; owner answers become follow-up task records owned by this agent.

evidence: Bounded context packet built with npm run agents:context -- --task SOCIAL-001; packet reported 16/45 candidate files within the 60,000-character budget and recorded all evidence-based scope expansions.

No production source or Supabase migration paths were changed; edits were limited to Social audit/state/backlog documents and the SOCIAL-001 control-plane record.
Final npm run agents:validate — validated 17 agents, 93 tasks, 0 warnings, 0 errors after SOCIAL-001 moved to completed and the task index refreshed.
Final checkpoint summary surfaces the five highest-priority Social owner/release questions and points to docs/engineering/agents/social/QUESTIONS.md.

checkpoints.summary: Full social domain audit completed. Read all library/service/hook/page files in the social scope. Produced BASELINE.md (comprehensive inventory), GAPS.md (30 gaps triaged), QUESTIONS.md (12 prioritized questions). Key findings: (1) /feed redirects to /news — social feed library has no visible consumer, (2) Groups are shells (CRUD only, no content/members/roles), (3) Messaging has no realtime, (4) Notifications are mature but fragmented across 4 surfaces (Phase 4 unification not started), (5) Collaboration redirects to artist domain. Top 5 blocking questions: Q1 Feed page architecture, Q2 Groups scope, Q3 Messaging realtime, Q4 Collaboration ownership, Q7 should_send_notification RPC verification.
